To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 2-subjet thrust distribution is Q independent for Q greater than or equal to 400 GeV and that the Q=∂ and Q=0 limits are related by e to next-to-leading order.

the 2-subjet distribution in boosted Z→qq(over bar) is well described by a next-to-leading order calculation at Q=∞, that this description breaks down at Q=0 due to jet contamination, and that the 1/Q corrections to Q=∞ from jet contamination are small.

the QCD calculation of the 2-sub-jettiness distribution for boosted Z → qq[over ¯ ] events at the Lhc is simplified by boosting to the Z center of mass frame and using known results for the e(+)e(−) thrust distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of jet substructure observables in the limit of large jet radius and large momentum transfer.
the study of the structure of hadronic final states produced in high energy proton-proton collisions.
the study of the structure of jets, which are collimated sprays of particles produced in high energy collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2-subjet thrust is a good variable for boosted Z→jj events at the LEC, but that it is not as good as the 2-subjets event shape, because of the large contamination from the underlying event.
the Q=∼400 GeV distribution is the most robust, and that this can be used to make a precise measurement of the Z→qq[ over ¯] cross section at the LHC.
the 2-subjetness distribution is QCD calculable, and can be used as a tool to probe the dynamics of the underlying hard process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thrust distribution is the same as the 2-sub-jetness distribution, but the former is in a boosted frame and the latter is not.

we have developed a new approach for calculating jet substructure at large Q, which is applicable to many observables, and is valid for a wide range of jet sizes, including the limit of small jet radius.
the thrust distribution in boosted event shapes can be used for jet substructure at the LHC, and the thrust distribution in QCD can be used to study the structure of the QCD Lagrangian.
The main takeaway from our work is that
jet substructure distributions are calculable to arbitrary precision, which will be essential for future searches and studies.
the thrust event shape is not just a toy example, but a powerful tool for precision studies of jet substructure.
jet substructure distributions at large Q can be systematically computed in perturbative QCD, with a small number of 1/Q corrections.
